title: Using LLMs to Secure Source Code — Eugene Yan, Anthropic
talk_summary: Eugene Yan describes a six-step agentic security harness (threat model, sandbox, discovery, verification, triage, patching) that Anthropic and partner teams use to find and fix vulnerabilities at scale. The core lesson is that discovery is now cheap and the real bottlenecks are verification, triage, patching, and human attention, so harness design should separate recall-optimized discovery from precision-optimized adversarial verification.

takeaways.technique: Separate discovery and adversarial verification agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Run discovery agents that optimize for recall, then hand only the finding (no reasoning trace) to an independent verification agent that assumes it is false and tries to disprove it, optionally by detonating a PoC in a fresh container.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when the discovery agent is trying to verify its own work in the loop... it may actually self censor and this may actually hurt recall
takeaways.numbers: true positive rate ~100% for a pentest team that gave the model tools to verify in the loop; 90% TP with a well-documented threat model

takeaways.technique: Write down the threat model / system context as a document
takeaways.what_they_do: Bootstrap a threat-model doc from code, commits, past patches, and interviews with the system expert, capturing implicit context (compensating controls, internal-only services, sensitive data) that is not in the code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model has great context of the code but poor context of the system
takeaways.numbers: well-documented threat model raises true positive rate to 90%

takeaways.what_they_do: With each stronger model, cut prompt size ~50% and replace prescriptive checklists with a single high-level instruction (e.g. 'look for where untrusted data hits the trust boundary').
takeaways.evidence_quote: as models get better, you actually need to remove from your prompts... I actually have to cut my prompt size by maybe about 50%

takeaways.technique: Give review agents executable tools, not just the diff
takeaways.what_they_do: Equip agents with tools to query APIs, read logs, read source, and run commands so they can confirm findings in the loop instead of speculating from code alone.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Allow the model to be dynamic to read the tools uh to to run the tools. And when they did this, their true positive rate was almost 100%

takeaways.technique: Ladder of patch validation with re-attack
takeaways.what_they_do: Validate a patch in stages: original PoC must fail, existing tests stay green, then a fresh discovery agent re-attacks the patched code to check the fix is comprehensive; feed that feedback back to the patcher.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have a fresh discovery agent try to attack the patch code again is the patch comprehensive enough

takeaways.technique: Triage and route findings to owners, not a firehose
takeaways.what_they_do: Deduplicate and cluster findings, score severity by impact magnitude and likelihood using business context, and route to code/service owners; avoid sending medium/low findings that burn engineer attention.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can lose trust with product engineers by sending them all the vulnerabilities that are true, even those that are medium or low severity
